hypotheses.claim: A refreshed Clerk token with the same sid should continue the existing authorized PTY lease without reconnecting or losing input.
hypotheses.falsifier: Across a frozen exact-source cohort, valid same-sid refreshes intermittently lose authorization, detach the socket, redirect input or fail to observe output.

hypotheses.claim: The PTY path may bind continuity to per-token jti/iat/exp or an old auth object instead of stable sid plus authorized user, making normal refresh appear as a new or stale lease holder.
hypotheses.falsifier: Traces show stable sid, changing jti, correct monotonic lease extension and invariant PTY ownership across every pass and fail, with the failure localized elsewhere.

hypotheses.claim: Suite scheduling sometimes places attach, blocking read or input near Clerk's short token/refresh boundary, so the same test crosses different auth epochs depending on load.
hypotheses.falsifier: Controlled offsets from token issue/expiry and injected scheduler/DB load produce no outcome dependence, while failures reproduce at invariant phases.

hypotheses.claim: The PTY failure depends on prior tests, shared tmux/session state, open database connections or cleanup timing rather than the refresh protocol itself.
hypotheses.falsifier: Isolated repetitions fail at the same rate as randomized-order full-suite arms after unique namespaces and verified cleanup.

hypotheses.claim: ZIELE and letzter-lauf are generated from different cached/run identities, allowing a newer document to resurrect an older green result.
hypotheses.falsifier: Both artifacts are proven to derive from one immutable run_id and identical result digest despite their divergent counts.

new_concepts.name: Authentication Epoch Continuity
new_concepts.definition: A long-lived PTY identity survives short-lived JWT rotation when stable session and user identity remain authorized.

new_concepts.name: Token-Lease Epoch Conflation
new_concepts.definition: A resource lease is accidentally keyed to a rotating token instance rather than the durable authenticated session.

new_concepts.name: Refresh-Phase Aliasing
new_concepts.definition: A test outcome changes because operations land on different sides of a periodic credential-refresh boundary.

new_concepts.name: Later-Stale Resurrection
new_concepts.definition: A document generated after the latest measurement nevertheless republishes an older result because consumer provenance is forked.

new_concepts.name: Pass-on-Retry Credit Trap
new_concepts.definition: A transient green result is misclassified as a fix even though no exact-source causal change or stable repetition supports it.
